objectives.description: Verify Lake's write pattern (atomic rename) in the reference consumer repo
Verify the .claude/ hardlink-vs-symlink fact and PROJECT_ROOT resolution
Verify the specs/ tracked, HEAD-stale fact
Measure free-space headroom, pick floor and cap values
Record all findings in the plan file

approaches_tried.approach: used bash --dir flag on lake-build-guard.sh while cwd differed from target dir
approaches_tried.reason: discovered guard resolves lock/result paths via --dir but never cd's before invoking lake itself; lake then searched upward from the wrong PWD. Worked around by cd'ing into the target dir directly (matches real dispatch usage where the agent's cwd is the worktree) and using --no-share to bypass the stale replayed result from the failed attempt.

deviations.description: Confirm a symlinked .claude/ does the opposite (makes PROJECT_ROOT resolve to the main tree)
deviations.reason: Empirically the symlink case did NOT resolve PROJECT_ROOT to the main tree under this bash version (5.3.9) -- both symlink and hardlink resolved to the worktree via the exact common_repo_root cd+pwd idiom. Recorded the disproof and a corrected, still-valid rationale for hardlink-over-symlink (ephemeral runtime-state bleed, not PROJECT_ROOT resolution) rather than silently keeping the disproven claim.
deviations.annotation: *(completed: no-.claude/ fact confirmed; PROJECT_ROOT-resolves-to-worktree confirmed for the hardlink case; the symlink-defeats-resolution mechanism did NOT reproduce on this bash -- see the corrected rationale in Phase 1 Findings -- hardlink-only decision stands for a different, verified reason)*
